correctness.rationale: After one outside element is conjugated into the prime complement, every remaining quotient exponent can be cancelled by a power of that baseline element. The remaining data are one kernel vector per generator. Since ℓ has prime order and ℓ-order scalar α satisfies F_p(α)=F_q, generation is exactly F_q-spanning. This proves d(G)=t+1 and yields the three pair cases: linear independence in the kernel, universal cross adjacency, and distinct conjugate-complement blocks outside. The packaged checker reconstructs the 48-vertex case directly from all generating triples.

value.rationale: The theorem addresses an explicit open degree-divisibility question on a nonnilpotent family with arbitrarily large minimum generator number, beyond the already-known 2-generated case. It determines the entire graph, not merely divisibility, and exposes two reusable geometries: projective lines in the kernel and conjugate-complement blocks outside.
